title: Design: Card shows Bill Invoices To without Change for a user without AP/AR
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as a user whose role has 'Customers → Create & Edit' but not 'View and Manage AP/AR Data' (for example the Foreman role), at the test location.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Have (set up by an Admin) customer A (it pays for others) and customer B, with customer A saved as customer B's Bill Invoices To in Edit Customer.
  • Open the attached pictures bt-p1-22-after-customer-page.png, bt-p1-24-after-edit-customer.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open customer B's page.
  2. Click the edit icon on customer B's card.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Under IBS the card shows "Bill Invoices To" and customer A's name, with no "Change".

Step 2:

  • Edit Customer opens with no Bill Invoices To field and no help line.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Bill To", Confluence 1003585538, version 0.5 (6 Nov 2026, pending approval, Chris Ward), read 9 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-12289, story SV-12303 (Story 1, Saved default Bill To on the customer page), story SV-12304 (Story 2, Bill Invoices To in New Customer and Edit Customer)

  • S1-N2: “Without 'Customers → Create & Edit' or 'View and Manage AP/AR Data', "Change" is hidden; the line still shows.”
  • S2-N1: “Without 'View and Manage AP/AR Data', the field is hidden and the window closes up around it.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Bill To design" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2prSHgwt2tWCz96QD2DWkd), version 1794239066-4906, read 9 Nov 2026: page "1 Set a customer's default Bill To", pictures "Customer page" (This build), "Edit Customer" (This build).

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • bt-p1-22-after-customer-page.png
  • bt-p1-24-after-edit-customer.png

The design's own words:

  • “She still sees "Bill Invoices To", "A & J Truck & Trailer Repair", with no "Change".”

One attached production picture is 1600 pixels wide although its note says 1440 x 1300; compare the fields, not the width.
